title: A patient's request overrides a prescriber's direction to withhold a Medication Guide
subtopic: Prescriber direction against a Medication Guide
rule_summary: If the licensed practitioner who prescribes a drug product subject to 21 CFR Part 208 determines that it is NOT IN A PARTICULAR PATIENT'S BEST INTEREST to receive a Medication Guide because of significant concerns about its effect, the practitioner MAY DIRECT that the Medication Guide not be provided to that patient. HOWEVER, the authorized dispenser SHALL PROVIDE A MEDICATION GUIDE TO ANY PATIENT WHO REQUESTS INFORMATION when the drug product is dispensed, REGARDLESS OF ANY SUCH DIRECTION by the licensed practitioner.
exam_relevance: A genuine conflict between a prescriber instruction and a patient request, resolved on the face of the regulation in the patient's favour.

authority.name: FDA Medication Guide exemptions and deferrals

exceptions: The practitioner's direction stands unless the patient requests information at the time the product is dispensed.
common_confusions: Treating the prescriber's direction as binding on the pharmacist without exception.
Reading the patient-request override as requiring a formal or written request.
Assuming the override lets the dispenser ignore the direction even where the patient asks for nothing.
verification_notes: Read verbatim in the current official publication on 2026-08-20 during Batch 3 tranche B3-F under Issue #91. A fresh independent legal and full-bank realism audit is still required before release.
